decisions.reason: The published forms.

decisions.choice: Assyria is "앗시리아" and Nineveh "니느웨"
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms; "앗수르" is not used for the empire.

source.text: וְרָבְצ֨וּ בְתוֹכָ֤הּ עֲדָרִים֙ כָּל־חַיְתוֹ־ג֔וֹי גַּם־קָאַת֙ גַּם־קִפֹּ֔ד בְּכַפְתֹּרֶ֖יהָ יָלִ֑ינוּ ק֠וֹל יְשׁוֹרֵ֤ר בַּֽחַלּוֹן֙ חֹ֣רֶב בַּסַּ֔ף כִּ֥י אַרְזָ֖ה עֵרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And herds will lie down in her midst, every beast of a nation; both [the] desert owl and [the] hedgehog will lodge in her capitals; a voice will sing in the window, desolation [will be] on the threshold, for he has laid bare the cedar-work.

en.L: And herds will lie down in her midst, every beast of the nations; \q both the desert owl and the hedgehog \q will lodge on her capitals; \q a voice will sing in the window, desolation [will be] on the threshold, \q for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has laid bare the cedar work.
en.B: Flocks will lie down in her, animals of every kind; \q the desert owl and the hedgehog \q will roost on the tops of her pillars. \q Their call will sound through the windows, rubble will lie on the doorsteps, \q for her cedar paneling has been stripped bare.
en.R: Herds of animals of every kind will lie down there. \q Desert owls and hedgehogs \q will sleep on top of the broken columns. \q Birds will call from the windows, and the doorways will be full of rubble. \q The cedar wood on the walls will be torn away.

es.L: Y se echarán en medio de ella rebaños, toda bestia de las naciones; \q tanto el búho del desierto como el erizo \q pasarán la noche en sus capiteles; \q una voz cantará en la ventana, desolación [habrá] en el umbral, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha dejado al desnudo el maderamen de cedro.
es.B: En medio de ella se echarán los rebaños, animales de toda clase; \q el búho del desierto y el erizo \q dormirán sobre los capiteles de sus columnas. \q Su canto resonará por las ventanas, habrá escombros en los umbrales, \q porque sus paneles de cedro han quedado al descubierto.
es.R: Allí se echarán manadas de animales de toda clase. \q Búhos del desierto y erizos \q dormirán encima de las columnas rotas. \q Las aves cantarán desde las ventanas, y las entradas estarán llenas de escombros. \q La madera de cedro de las paredes será arrancada.

fr.L: Et des troupeaux se coucheront au milieu d’elle, toutes les bêtes des nations ; \q le hibou du désert aussi bien que le hérisson \q passeront la nuit sur ses chapiteaux ; \q une voix chantera à la fenêtre, la désolation [sera] sur le seuil, \q car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a mis à nu les boiseries de cèdre.
fr.B: Des troupeaux se coucheront chez elle, des bêtes de toute espèce ; \q le hibou du désert et le hérisson \q nicheront sur le haut de ses colonnes. \q Leur cri résonnera par les fenêtres, les décombres joncheront les seuils, \q car ses lambris de cèdre ont été arrachés.
fr.R: Des troupeaux d’animaux de toutes sortes s’y coucheront. \q Les hiboux du désert et les hérissons \q dormiront en haut des colonnes brisées. \q Les oiseaux crieront aux fenêtres, et les entrées seront pleines de décombres. \q Le bois de cèdre des murs sera arraché.

sw.L: Na makundi yatalala katikati yake, kila mnyama wa mataifa; \q bundi wa jangwani na nungunungu \q watakaa juu ya vichwa vya nguzo zake; \q sauti itaimba dirishani, ukiwa [utakuwa] kizingitini, \q kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ameziacha wazi kazi za mierezi.
sw.B: Makundi ya wanyama yatalala ndani yake, wanyama wa kila aina; \q bundi wa jangwani na nungunungu \q watatua juu ya vichwa vya nguzo zake. \q Milio yao itasikika madirishani, kifusi kitalala vizingitini, \q kwa maana mbao zake za mierezi zimeondolewa.
sw.R: Makundi ya wanyama wa kila aina yatalala huko. \q Bundi wa jangwani na nungunungu \q watalala juu ya nguzo zilizovunjika. \q Ndege watalia madirishani, na milango itajaa kifusi. \q Mbao za mierezi zilizokuwa ukutani zitang'olewa.

vi.L: Các bầy thú sẽ nằm giữa nó, mọi loài thú của các dân; \q cả cú sa mạc lẫn nhím \q sẽ ngủ trên các đầu cột của nó; \q một tiếng hót trong cửa sổ, sự hoang tàn [ở] nơi ngưỡng cửa, \q vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã lột trần đồ gỗ bá hương.
vi.B: Các bầy thú sẽ nằm nghỉ giữa thành, đủ mọi loài thú; \q cú sa mạc và nhím \q sẽ đậu trên đầu những cây cột của nó. \q Tiếng chúng kêu vang qua cửa sổ, gạch vụn nằm đầy ngưỡng cửa, \q vì gỗ bá hương ốp tường đã bị lột trần.
vi.R: Đủ mọi loài thú sẽ nằm nghỉ ở đó. \q Cú sa mạc và nhím \q sẽ ngủ trên đầu những cây cột gãy đổ. \q Chim chóc kêu ngoài cửa sổ, và các lối vào đầy gạch vụn. \q Gỗ bá hương ốp trên tường sẽ bị giật xuống.

ko.L: 그 가운데 가축 떼가, 민족들의 온갖 짐승이 누울 것이다. \q 사막 올빼미와 고슴도치가 \q 그 기둥 머리들에서 잠잘 것이다. \q 창문에서 소리가 노래하고, 문지방에는 황폐함이 [있을 것이다]. \q 그분께서 백향목 판자를 벗겨 내셨기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그 가운데 양 떼와 온갖 짐승이 누울 것이다. \q 사막 올빼미와 고슴도치가 \q 그 기둥 꼭대기에 깃들 것이다. \q 새 소리가 창문에서 울리고, 문간에는 부서진 돌무더기가 쌓일 것이다. \q 그 성의 백향목 판자가 다 벗겨졌기 때문이다.
ko.R: 온갖 짐승 떼가 그곳에 누울 것이다. \q 사막 올빼미와 고슴도치가 \q 무너진 기둥 위에서 잠잘 것이다. \q 창문에서 새들이 울고, 문간은 무너진 돌로 가득할 것이다. \q 벽에 붙은 백향목 판자는 다 뜯겨 나갈 것이다.

decisions.choice: every beast of the nations: animals of every kind
alternatives: every wild animal of the field
decisions.reason: The phrase is unusual. It seems to mean all kinds of animals, as a nation is a kind of people. Some suggest a small change to read "every wild animal of the field".

decisions.choice: the desert owl and the hedgehog: creatures of ruins
decisions.reason: The same pair of creatures possesses ruined Edom in Isaiah 34:11, and the hedgehog ruined Babylon in Isaiah 14:23. The exact animals are uncertain; the second may be a kind of owl, which would fit their lodging on the pillars.

decisions.choice: desolation on the threshold: rubble lies in the doorways
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means "desolation" or "dryness". The Greek and Latin translations are generally said to read "ravens" (Hebrew 'orev for chorev, a difference of one letter), which would give a bird for the threshold to match the owl on the pillars and the voice in the window. The Hebrew text makes good sense, and is kept.

decisions.choice: capitals, cedar work: the remains of fine buildings
decisions.reason: The capitals are the carved tops of columns, now lying among the ruins or still standing. Cedar was used to panel palaces and temples (1 Kings 7:2-7; Jeremiah 22:14). When the roofs fall and the cedar is stripped, only the bare stone is left. "He" who laid it bare is the LORD, or the enemy he sends. |

decisions.choice: her cedar paneling has been stripped bare (B); will be torn away (R)
alternatives: he has laid bare the cedar work
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable leave the doer unnamed, because the verse does not say whether he is the LORD or the enemy (m4). Readable says "Birds will call" for "a voice will sing", which the line implies. |

decisions.choice: "el búho del desierto y el erizo"
decisions.reason: The creatures of ruins keep the Spanish of Isaiah 34:11, where the same pair appears.

decisions.choice: "le hibou du désert" (L, B, R) for *qaʾat*
decisions.reason: The bird is uncertain; French follows the English "desert owl", a creature of ruins.

decisions.choice: "mwari na nungunungu" (L), "mwari wa jangwani" (B), "bundi wa jangwani" (R)
decisions.reason: The pair as published in Isaiah 34:11 at each level; the creatures are uncertain (m2).

decisions.choice: Nineveh is "nó" at every level
decisions.reason: The terms note: a city is "nó"; the Hebrew feminine is not carried into Vietnamese except for Zion.

decisions.choice: "사막 올빼미와 고슴도치"
decisions.reason: The pair as published in Isaiah 34:11. Literal gives the one who stripped the cedar -시-, reading him as the LORD (m4); Balanced and Readable leave the doer unnamed, as the English does.

source.text: זֹ֞֠אתהָעִ֤יר הָעַלִּיזָה֙ הַיּוֹשֶׁ֣בֶת לָבֶ֔טַח הָאֹֽמְרָה֙ בִּלְבָבָ֔הּ אֲנִ֖י וְאַפְסִ֣י ע֑וֹד אֵ֣יךְ׀הָיְתָ֣ה לְשַׁמָּ֗ה מַרְבֵּץ֙ לַֽחַיָּ֔ה כֹּ֚ל עוֹבֵ֣ר עָלֶ֔יהָ יִשְׁרֹ֖ק יָנִ֥יעַ יָדֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: This [is] the exultant city that dwelt in security, that said in her heart, I [am], and there is none besides me still. How she has become a desolation, a lair for beasts! Everyone passing by her will hiss, will shake his hand.

en.L: This [is] the exultant city \q that dwelt in security, \q that said in her heart, "I [am], and there is none but me still." \q How she has become a desolation, a lair for wild animals! \q Everyone who passes by her \q will hiss and shake {{gender:their|his}} hand.
en.B: This is the city that exulted, \q that lived without a care, \q that thought in her heart, "I am, and there is no other but me." \q What a ruin she has become, a place where wild animals lie down! \q Everyone who passes by her \q hisses and shakes {{gender:their|his}} fist.
en.R: This is the proud city that felt so safe. \q It told itself, "I am the one, and there is no one else." \q But now look! It has become a ruin where wild animals rest. \q All who pass by will make fun of it \q and shake their fists at it.

es.L: Esta [es] la ciudad alegre \q que habitaba confiada, \q que decía en su corazón: «Yo [soy], y fuera de mí no hay nadie más». \q ¡Cómo ha quedado hecha una desolación, una guarida de fieras! \q Todo el que pase junto a ella \q silbará y agitará su mano.
es.B: Esta es la ciudad que se divertía, \q que vivía sin preocupaciones, \q que pensaba en su corazón: «Yo soy, y no hay otra fuera de mí». \q ¡En qué ruina se ha convertido, en guarida de animales salvajes! \q Todo el que pasa junto a ella \q silba y agita el puño.
es.R: Esta es la ciudad orgullosa que se sentía tan segura. \q Se decía: «Yo soy la única, y no hay nadie más». \q ¡Pero {{plural_you:miren|mirad}} ahora! Se ha convertido en ruinas donde descansan los animales salvajes. \q Todos los que pasen se burlarán de ella \q y le mostrarán el puño.

fr.L: Voilà la ville exultante \q qui habitait en sécurité, \q qui disait dans son cœur : « Moi, [je suis], et il n’y a encore personne d’autre que moi. » \q Comme elle est devenue une désolation, un repaire pour les bêtes sauvages ! \q Quiconque passe près d’elle \q sifflera et agitera la main.
fr.B: Voilà la ville qui exultait, \q qui vivait sans souci, \q qui pensait : « Moi, je suis, et il n’y en a pas d’autre que moi. » \q Quelle ruine elle est devenue, un gîte pour les bêtes sauvages ! \q Tous ceux qui passent près d’elle \q sifflent et montrent le poing.
fr.R: Voilà la ville orgueilleuse qui se sentait si en sécurité. \q Elle se disait : « Je suis la seule, et il n’y a personne d’autre. » \q Mais maintenant, regardez ! Elle est devenue une ruine où se reposent les bêtes sauvages. \q Tous ceux qui passeront se moqueront d’elle \q et lui montreront le poing.

sw.L: Huu [ndio] mji uliojaa shangwe \q uliokaa salama, \q uliosema moyoni mwake, "Mimi [ndiye], wala hakuna mwingine ila mimi." \q Jinsi ulivyokuwa ukiwa, makao ya wanyama wa porini! \q Kila apitaye karibu nao \q atauzomea na kutikisa mkono wake.
sw.B: Huu ndio mji uliokuwa ukishangilia, \q uliokaa bila wasiwasi, \q uliowaza moyoni mwake, "Mimi ndiye, wala hakuna mwingine ila mimi." \q Umekuwa magofu kama nini, mahali wanyama wa porini wanapolala! \q Kila apitaye karibu nao \q anauzomea na kuutikisia ngumi yake.
sw.R: Huu ndio mji wenye kiburi uliojiona uko salama. \q Ulijiambia, "Mimi ndiye, wala hakuna mwingine." \q Lakini sasa tazama! Umekuwa magofu ambamo wanyama wa porini wanapumzika. \q Wote wanaopita karibu nao watauzomea \q na kuutikisia ngumi zao.

vi.L: Đây [là] thành hớn hở \q đã sống an ổn, \q đã nói trong lòng: "Ta [là], và ngoài ta chẳng còn ai." \q Sao nó đã trở thành hoang vu, hang ổ cho thú rừng! \q Mọi kẻ đi ngang qua nó \q sẽ huýt gió và vẫy tay.
vi.B: Đây là thành từng hớn hở, \q từng sống vô tư lự, \q từng nghĩ trong lòng: "Ta đây, và ngoài ta chẳng có ai khác." \q Nó đã thành đống đổ nát, nơi thú rừng nằm nghỉ! \q Mọi kẻ đi ngang qua nó \q đều huýt gió và vung nắm tay.
vi.R: Đây là thành kiêu ngạo từng cảm thấy thật an toàn. \q Nó tự nhủ: "Chỉ có ta mà thôi, chẳng có ai khác." \q Nhưng giờ hãy xem! Nó đã thành đống đổ nát, nơi thú rừng nằm nghỉ. \q Mọi người đi ngang qua sẽ chế giễu nó \q và vung nắm tay về phía nó.

ko.L: 이것이 기뻐 뛰놀던 성읍, \q 안심하고 살던 [성읍이다]. \q 그 성읍은 마음속으로 "나다. 나 외에는 아무도 없다" 하고 말했다. \q 어찌하여 황무지가, 들짐승의 굴이 되었는가! \q 그곳을 지나가는 자마다 \q 비웃으며 손을 흔들 것이다.
ko.B: 이것이 우쭐대던 성읍, \q 아무 걱정 없이 살던 성읍이다. \q 그 성읍은 속으로 "나뿐이다. 나 말고는 아무도 없다" 하고 생각했다. \q 그런데 어찌하여 이렇게 폐허가 되어 들짐승이 눕는 곳이 되었는가! \q 그곳을 지나가는 사람마다 \q 비웃으며 주먹을 흔든다.
ko.R: 이것이 그토록 안전하다고 뽐내던 교만한 성읍이다. \q 그 성읍은 속으로 "나만 대단하다. 나 말고는 아무도 없다" 하고 말했다. \q 그러나 보아라! 이제는 들짐승이 쉬는 폐허가 되었다. \q 지나가는 사람마다 그 성읍을 비웃으며 \q 주먹을 휘두를 것이다.

decisions.choice: I am, and there is none but me: the words of Babylon in Isaiah 47:8, 10
decisions.reason: Isaiah 47:8 and 10 put the same words in the mouth of Babylon, the proud city that thought it could never fall. They are words that belong to God alone (Isaiah 45:5-6, 18), so the city claims for itself what is God's. Nineveh, which said them first, falls before Babylon does. |

decisions.choice: hiss and shake the hand: gestures of scorn and horror at a ruin
decisions.reason: Passers-by hiss or whistle and shake their hands at a ruined city, in horror and in mockery (Jeremiah 19:8; 49:17; Lamentations 2:15). |

decisions.choice: this is the exultant city: a taunt over the fallen city
decisions.reason: The verse is spoken as if Nineveh had already fallen, a mocking lament over a city that boasted of its safety. |

decisions.choice: I [am], and there is none but me still (L); I am, and there is no other but me (B); I am the one, and there is no one else (R)
decisions.reason: Where Zephaniah uses the words of Isaiah 47:8, each level uses the wording already published there. The gender setting gives "their" for the passer-by, man or woman; Readable makes the passers-by plural. Readable says "make fun of it" for "hiss", as Jeremiah 19:8 does. |

decisions.choice: the Spanish wording of Isaiah 47:8
decisions.reason: Nineveh's boast repeats Babylon's in Isaiah 47:8, 10, and the Spanish reuses those words at each level. "Su" covers both sexes, so there is no gender span where the English has one.

decisions.choice: The published Isaiah 47:8 words for the boast at each level
decisions.reason: Nineveh's boast is Babylon's in Isaiah 47:8, 10; French reuses the published Isaiah's words, and the city takes feminine agreement throughout, as the term sheet asks.

decisions.choice: "Mimi [ndiye], wala hakuna mwingine ila mimi" (L); "Mimi ndiye, wala hakuna mwingine ila mimi" (B); "Mimi ndiye, wala hakuna mwingine" (R)
decisions.reason: The city's boast is Babylon's in Isaiah 47:8, so each level reuses that verse's published Swahili. "Wake" covers everyone, so there is no gender span where the English has one.

decisions.choice: the Vietnamese wording of Isaiah 47:8 for the city's boast ("Ta [là], và ngoài ta chẳng còn ai" L; "Ta đây, và ngoài ta chẳng có ai khác" B; "Chỉ có ta mà thôi, chẳng có ai khác" R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision: Nineveh speaks Babylon's words in Isaiah 47:8, 10; the published Vietnamese is reused. The city's "ta" is lowercase and takes no span.

decisions.choice: "I am, and there is none but me" reuses the Korean Isaiah 47:8 at each level ("나다. 나 외에는 아무도 없다" L; "나뿐이다. 나 말고는 아무도 없다" B; "나만 대단하다. 나 말고는 아무도 없다" R)
decisions.reason: Nineveh says what Babylon says in Isaiah 47:8, 10, so the published words are kept. The city is "그 성읍", never "그녀", as the term sheet asks; no gender span is needed for "지나가는 자마다".

decisions.choice: "Quiconque … agitera la main" (L), "Tous ceux qui … montrent le poing" (B), no gender span where the English has {{gender:their|his}}
decisions.reason: French generic "quiconque" and "tous ceux qui" are already inclusive, and the possessive is not needed; the style guide puts no gender setting on pronouns.

decisions.choice: no gender span for "his hand"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese needs no possessive here ("vẫy tay"), so the English gender span has no counterpart.
